statement: For every integer q >= 2 with gcd(q,6)=1 and every nonempty R subset of Z/qZ, if A_N={1 <= n <= N : n mod q lies in R} and M(A) counts signed ordered pairs (x,d) with d != 0 and x,x+d,x+3d in A, then the limit L(q,R)=lim_{N->infinity} M(A_N)/|A_N|^2 exists, satisfies L(q,R) <= 1/3, and equals 1/3 if and only if R is a coset of an additive subgroup of Z/qZ. More precisely, L(q,R)=T_q(R)/(3|R|^2), where T_q(R)=#{(u,v) in (Z/qZ)^2 : u,u+v,u+3v in R}.
contribution: A complete elementary proof of the frozen original claim: separate fixed-residue lattice sums over the positive and negative dilation triangles establish the exact limiting reduction, including nonzero dilations congruent to zero modulo q; a bijection bounds the modular count by |R|^2; and invertibility of 2 and 3 classifies equality exactly as additive-subgroup cosets. No novelty or acceptance claim is made.
